title: Basavanna's vachana on rituals
body:
Read the following vachana composed by Basavanna, the leader of the Virashaiva movement in Karnataka, and answer the question that follows.

When they see a serpent carved in stone they pour milk on it.
If a real serpent comes they say: "Kill. Kill."
To the servant of the god who could eat if served they say: "Go away! Go away!"
But to the image of the god which cannot eat they offer dishes of food.

title: Declining a royal gift
body:
Read the following account from a sufi text describing the proceedings at Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya's hospice in 1313, recorded by Amir Hasan Sijzi, and answer the question that follows.

A local ruler had sent the Shaikh the deed of ownership to two gardens and much land, along with provisions and tools for their maintenance, giving up all his rights to them. The master did not accept the gift and lamented: "What have I to do with gardens and fields and lands? None of our spiritual masters had engaged in such activity." He then told a story: Ulugh Khan (later Sultan Ghiyasuddin) had offered Shaikh Fariduddin some money and ownership deeds for four villages. Smiling, the Shaikh said: "Give me the money. I will dispense it to the dervishes. But as for those land deeds, keep them. There are many who long for them. Give them away to such persons."
